title: Phase-gated Minimum Slate & Skill-throttle for Cycle Capacity
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: Introduce a phase-gated minimum-slate (MinSlate) policy plus a skill-throttle mechanism to reduce cycle overcommit, make mid-cycle scope cuts less painful, and improve cross-team predictability. MinSlate defines a guaranteed minimal set of committed items that receive protected staffing and rollout attention. Skill-throttle enforces hard caps on concurrently committed work that requires scarce skills (ML infra, runtime kernel, security/compliance) and surfaces forced de-scopes early. The combination aims to preserve delivery of critical customer-facing outcomes while making capacity allocation explicit and auditable.
acceptance_criteria: MinSlate policy doc published with worked examples and approval from Eng, Design, & PM leads
Skill-throttle enforcement implemented as a Confluence checklist + linear tag workflow in pilot teams
Pilot cycle (2026-W10) shows >= 20% fewer mid-cycle scope drops on pilot initiatives compared to baseline
Dashboard with per-skill concurrency, protected slots, and projected burn published in Console for stakeholders
Rollout playbook with 'override' flow and escalation path documented for emergency work

decisions: Use a three-tier MinSlate: Critical (customer SLO/regulatory), Core (high-business-impact), Opportunistic (nice-to-have).
Skill-throttle counts unique active tickets requiring a skill tag; threshold defaults: Critical=3, Core=6 for the pilot.
Enforcement is soft during pilot (alerts + weekly review) before automating hard-blocks in Q3 2026.
Overrides allowed only with written approval from Eng lead + PM partner and recorded in the cycle playbook.
Pilot teams: Runtime, Dedicated Capacity, Console. Expand after successful metrics and retrospective.
risks: Teams may game labels to bypass throttle; mitigation: add periodic audit and tie to PR metadata.
Protected slots could starve support/maintenance work; mitigation: reserve float capacity and rotate protection every cycle.
Initial dashboard telemetry may undercount cross-skill work (e.g., infra+security); mitigation: include multi-tag aggregation in prototype.
If enforcement is too strict, velocity could drop and cause missed OKRs; mitigation: staged rollout with manual overrides and close monitoring.
